key: Think of a newspaper archive.
name: ch00_newspaper_archive
alt: A newspaper office where a clerk files incoming stories in a back room while a librarian cuts clippings into index cards for a fast lookup cabinet.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated cutaway view of an old Indian newspaper office, read left to right in three zones. On the far left, three bundles of typed stories arrive through a mail slot from different bureaus, each tied with a different coloured string, and a thin, bespectacled clerk in his fifties wearing a cream half-sleeve shirt gathers them into a wire basket. In the middle zone, a dim back room lined with tall steel shelves holds stacks of untouched original newspapers in brown files, the clerk sliding one more file onto a shelf. On the right, under a bright desk lamp, a cheerful librarian in her thirties in a green cotton saree and reading glasses sits at a wide wooden table cutting a story into neat rectangular clippings with long scissors; beside her, small white index cards are each pinned to a clipping, and she drops them into a compact wooden card cabinet with many small drawers. A curved dotted arrow runs from the mail slot to the back room to her table to the cabinet. In a small round inset above the cabinet, a reader asks for one topic and a single drawer slides open with the right card. Warm tungsten light, paper dust in the air, calm and orderly mood. Labels: "CRAWLER" under the clerk with the wire basket, "DATA WAREHOUSE" on the back-room shelves, "VECTOR DB" on the card cabinet.

key: A chai stall at a railway station. Onlin
name: ch00_chai_stall_three_modes
alt: A railway-station chai stall serving a hurried passenger, preparing a delivery order and filling a big batch of cups for a canteen contract.
scene: A wide, eye-level view of a busy chai stall on an Indian railway platform, composed as one continuous scene with three clear zones. In the centre the chaiwala, a lean man in his forties with a checked lungi, rolled sleeves and a towel over his shoulder, pours steaming tea in a high arc from a brass kettle into a small glass. LEFT zone: at the front window a young passenger in a hurry, backpack on, one hand reaching for the glass while glancing over his shoulder at a blue train whose doors are open and a platform clock showing two minutes to departure. MIDDLE-BACK zone: a teenage helper in a vest packs six sealed paper cups into a cloth bag, a phone on the counter shows a chat bubble with a cup icon, and a bicycle waits by the stall ready for delivery. RIGHT zone: at the back, a large steel urn and rows of stacked paper cups being filled on big trays, with a small wall clock showing four o'clock. A brass milk can sits by the stove with a small tasting spoon resting on its lid. Morning platform light with steam rising, lively but organised mood. Labels: "ONLINE" above the hurried passenger, "ASYNC" above the delivery helper, "BATCH" above the stacked cups.

key: A mimicry artist on a comedy show
name: ch01_mimicry_artist
alt: A mimicry artist on stage perfectly imitates a cricket commentator but is blank when asked what the commentator says at a family dinner.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, the same mimicry artist in both halves: a stocky man in his thirties with a neat moustache, wearing a sequined blue blazer. LEFT panel: on a bright comedy-show stage with spotlights and a small studio audience laughing, he leans forward in a confident commentator pose, one hand cupping a headset microphone; behind him a large TV screen shows a cricket broadcast with a batsman mid-shot, and a dotted line runs from the screen into the artist's head, showing he learned only from the broadcast. RIGHT panel: the same man stands awkwardly at a warm family dining table with plates of rotis, dal and rice, an elderly aunt in a shawl turning to him expectantly with a serving spoon raised; he is frozen mid-word with a blank, sweating face, and a thought bubble above him is completely empty except for a small question mark. A faint outline of the real commentator, in casual home clothes, laughs at the head of the table. Left side lit with harsh stage spotlights, right side lit with soft yellow household light; amused yet slightly awkward mood. Labels: "BROADCAST SIDE" at the top of the left panel, "NO DATA" next to the empty thought bubble.

key: A small kirana shop opening in a new col
name: ch01_kirana_mvp
alt: A small new kirana shop stocked only with everyday essentials, with a UPI scanner and a phone for WhatsApp orders, as a customer completes her shopping.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a small, freshly painted kirana shop opening in a new residential colony, with half-built apartment blocks and a cement mixer in the soft-focus background. A marigold garland hangs over the shutter for the opening day. The shelves are sparse but complete: sacks of rice, jars of dal, bottles of cooking oil, a small fridge with milk packets, and a row of biscuit packets; one wall section on the right is deliberately empty with a few bare brackets ready for a future shelf. The owner, a smiling man in his late thirties with a sleeveless sweater over a white shirt, hands a cloth bag to a young mother in a salwar kameez holding a toddler's hand; her bag shows rice, milk and biscuits, everything she needed. On the counter sit a printed QR code stand, a small phone showing a chat bubble with a shopping list, and a notebook. Outside, a faint dotted outline of a frozen-food cabinet and a delivery scooter are drawn in ghosted lines, showing what was intentionally left out. Bright morning sunlight, hopeful and modest mood. Labels: "MVP" on a small board above the shop, "ADD LATER" beside the empty brackets.

key: The TTE never phones the chart-making te
name: ch01_railway_chart_fti
alt: Three railway scenes: clerks preparing the reservation chart, a classroom training TTEs, and a TTE on the train checking a passenger's seat from the printed chart.
scene: A three-panel horizontal illustration separated by thin vertical lines, telling one Indian Railways story from left to right. LEFT panel: in a back office with tube lights, two clerks in their forties, one in a grey safari suit, print a long reservation chart on a dot-matrix printer and paste it onto a board; a stack of passenger slips lies beside them. MIDDLE panel: a small training classroom where a senior instructor with grey hair points to a rule chart on the wall while three young TTEs in black coats and white shirts take notes at wooden desks. RIGHT panel: inside a sleeper coach with blue berths, an experienced TTE in a black coat and name badge holds the printed chart on a clipboard and checks the ticket of a middle-aged passenger in a kurta sitting on his berth. A bold arrow runs from the printed chart in the left panel to the clipboard in the right panel, and another arrow runs from the classroom to the TTE's head. A disconnected old telephone lies on a shelf in the right panel with a small cross over its cord, showing the TTE never calls the chart team. Soft daylight through the coach windows, orderly mood. Labels: "FEATURE" above the left panel, "TRAINING" above the middle panel, "INFERENCE" above the right panel.

key: Vegetable chopping (data/feature work)
name: ch01_wedding_caterer_scaling
alt: At a wedding kitchen, many helpers chop vegetables, one huge biryani handi sits on a bigger stove, and more serving counters open for the guest queue.
scene: A wide, elevated view of a large outdoor wedding catering tent at dusk, strings of fairy lights overhead, read left to right in three zones. LEFT: a long row of six helpers in white vests and caps sit cross-legged chopping onions, tomatoes and coriander on wooden boards, with a seventh helper just arriving with his own board; small plus signs float above the newcomer. CENTRE: one enormous copper biryani handi, sealed with dough around the lid, sits on a wide, oversized gas stove; a head cook in his fifties with a big moustache and a white apron points proudly at it, while a smaller handi on a smaller stove is shown faded behind him, with an upward arrow showing the jump from small to big. RIGHT: a buffet area where a guest queue of men in kurtas and women in bright sarees grows, and a waiter in a maroon waistcoat pulls the cloth off a third serving counter to open it beside two busy counters. Sideways arrows run along the row of choppers and along the counters, and an upward arrow rises beside the handi. Warm golden lamp light, festive and busy mood. Labels: "SCALE OUT" above the row of choppers, "SCALE UP" above the giant handi, "SCALE OUT" above the serving counters.

key: each platform has its own fixed train
name: ch02_platform_python_version
alt: A railway station where platform 3 always has the 3.11.8 express and platform 1 has the station's default train, each marked by a platform board.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view across an Indian railway station with three parallel platforms receding to the right, a pedestrian overbridge arching above them. On platform 1 in the foreground, a plain grey local train waits under a hanging board reading "DEFAULT"; a few commuters stand casually. On platform 3 in the middle distance, a sleek blue-and-white express train waits under a bright yellow hanging board reading "3.11.8". A young software engineer in his twenties, wearing a hoodie and carrying a laptop bag, walks down the overbridge stairs onto platform 3 holding a small ticket that matches the yellow board; a dotted path traces his walk from the overbridge to the express door. At the foot of the stairs to platform 3 there is a small signpost shaped like a folder icon. Pigeons sit on the overbridge railings, a tea vendor with a kettle stands near platform 1, and steel benches line each platform. Bright late-morning light filtering through the station's corrugated roof, calm and orderly mood, the platforms clearly separated by tracks. Labels: "REPO FOLDER" on the folder-shaped signpost at platform 3, and "PLATFORM BOARD" with a small arrow pointing to the yellow hanging board.

key: is your mother's shopping note
name: ch02_shopping_note_vs_bill
alt: A mother's vague shopping note beside an exact kirana bill with brand and batch number, handed to the next shopper so the biryani tastes the same.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, inside a warm Indian home kitchen. LEFT panel: a mother in her fifties in a cotton saree, reading glasses on her head, hands a small torn page from a notebook to her teenage son; the note in her handwriting reads only "Rice 5 kg". The son looks confused, scratching his head, and a thought bubble above him shows three different rice sacks with question marks. RIGHT panel: the same son now holds a long printed kirana bill on thermal paper with a clear highlighted line reading "Batch 2311", and he hands it confidently to his younger cousin at the door who is about to go shopping; behind them a pot of biryani steams on the stove and the mother smiles approvingly. In the background of the right panel, three separate steel rice bins stand side by side, each with a small family-name tag, a lid firmly on each so one family's rice never mixes with another's. Soft morning light through a window with a small tulsi plant, cosy and domestic mood. Labels: "NOTE" at the top of the left panel, "LOCK FILE" at the top of the right panel, and "VENV" on the row of separate rice bins.

key: arrives with a whole kitchen in one truc
name: ch02_caterer_kitchen_truck
alt: A caterer's truck parks at a wedding venue and opens its doors to reveal a complete, ready-to-run kitchen inside.
scene: A wide, slightly low three-quarter view of a wedding venue lawn in the evening, marigold arches and a lit pandal in the background. In the foreground a medium-sized white catering truck is parked with its rear and side doors swung wide open, revealing a complete compact kitchen packed neatly inside: two gas stoves already lit with blue flames, rows of hanging steel ladles and kadais, a cold-storage cabinet with frosted glass, stacked steel plates and a water drum. A cheerful caterer in his forties wearing a white chef jacket and a red bandana stands on the truck's rear step, arms spread wide in a 'ready' gesture. Two helpers carry a large steaming vessel down a small ramp toward the buffet tables. In a small inset bubble at top left, the same truck is shown closed and driving along a highway, everything packed inside. Behind the truck, a dotted ghost outline of a much larger permanent banquet-hall kitchen is faintly drawn, hinting that the truck is a scaled-down version. Warm golden fairy lights and stove glow, festive and efficient mood. Labels: "DOCKER IMAGE" on the closed truck in the inset bubble, "UP" with a small arrow next to the swung-open doors.

key: An auto-rickshaw with the meter running
name: ch02_auto_meter_running
alt: An auto-rickshaw waits outside a shop with its meter ticking up while the passenger shops inside, and a friend calls when it crosses 500 rupees.
scene: A wide, eye-level street view in an Indian market, split by composition rather than lines. On the left, a classic yellow-and-green auto-rickshaw is parked at the kerb with its driver, a relaxed older man with a grey beard and a khaki uniform, dozing with his feet up on the handlebar. A large mechanical fare meter on the auto's side glows, and an inset magnified bubble shows its digits climbing past 500 with small motion lines. In the centre background, through a big glass shopfront of a saree showroom, the passenger, a young man in his late twenties with a laptop bag, browses shelves with his back to the street, completely unaware. On the right, a separate small inset shows his friend, a young woman in a kurta at her desk, calling him on her phone with an alarmed face and a bell icon beside her. A wall clock above the shop door shows a long time passing, with faint clock trails. Bright afternoon sun, slightly comic but warning mood. Labels: "ENDPOINT" on the parked auto-rickshaw, "BILLING ALARM" beside the friend calling, and a small sticker on the meter reading "₹500".

key: run its own morning trip to the mandi
name: ch03_mandi_morning_trip
alt: A restaurant cook visits several mandi stalls at dawn, then washes and sorts the produce and stacks it by type in a cold room.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated panoramic illustration read left to right as one morning journey. LEFT: a busy wholesale vegetable mandi at dawn, with three different stalls under tarpaulin roofs piled with tomatoes, onions and spinach; a young restaurant cook in his twenties in a white chef cap and checked shirt bargains at one stall while carrying a big woven basket already holding produce from the other two. A small delivery tempo with the restaurant's plain logo waits nearby. MIDDLE: at the back of the restaurant, two helpers wash vegetables in large steel tubs under a tap and sort them into labelled plastic crates. RIGHT: inside a cold room with frosted walls and blue light, neatly stacked crates by type, each crate's contents still whole and unchopped. A curved dotted arrow connects the three stalls to the basket, the basket to the washing tubs, and the tubs to the cold room. In a faded corner at the far left, a plastic packet of pre-cut vegetables sits ignored on a shelf, marked with a small cross. Soft pink dawn light turning into cool blue inside the cold room, fresh and purposeful mood. Labels: "SOURCES" above the three mandi stalls, "ETL" above the washing tubs, "WAREHOUSE" on the cold room door.

key: A courier delivery boy with a list of 25
name: ch03_courier_failed_and_move_on
alt: A courier on a scooter notes a failed delivery at a locked door and moves on to the next address, ending with a tally sheet per area.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a Bengaluru residential street with apartment buildings and gulmohar trees. In the foreground a courier delivery boy in his early twenties, wearing a branded-free red jacket, helmet pushed up, stands at the gate of a house whose door has a large padlock; he holds a clipboard and is writing a small cross next to one line, with a calm, unbothered face. His scooter behind him has a big carrier box with many parcels stacked. A dotted arrow leaves the locked house and continues down the street to the next house, where a smiling elderly man in a lungi receives a parcel. A ghosted, crossed-out arrow pointing back toward a distant warehouse shows he does not return everything. In a large inset bubble at the top right, his end-of-day clipboard sheet is shown up close with two short lines reading "Koramangala 8/8" and "Indiranagar 6/7", with a small red cross beside the second line. Bright late-morning sun with dappled tree shadows, brisk and practical mood. Labels: "FAILED" next to the padlocked door, "MOVE ON" along the dotted arrow to the next house.

key: Photocopying a friend's whole notebook
name: ch03_xerox_notebook
alt: A student photocopies a friend's whole notebook, copies only the useful pages into her own register at home, and throws the photocopies away.
scene: A three-step horizontal illustration read left to right, separated by soft curved arrows. LEFT: a cramped Xerox shop with a large photocopier spitting out warm pages, a shopkeeper in his fifties with reading glasses on a chain feeding a friend's notebook into it; a college student in her late teens, wearing a kurti, jeans and a sling bag, waits with a thick stack of photocopies. MIDDLE: at her home study desk under a table lamp, she sits with the photocopy stack on the left and her own neat ruled register open on the right, copying only the pages with dense notes; pages with doodles of cartoon faces and a printed class timetable are pushed aside. A small magnified bubble shows her handwriting written very tightly with no gaps between words, hinting that spacing is squeezed out. RIGHT: she drops the remaining photocopies into a waste-paper basket beside the desk, the register closed and tidy under her arm. Warm evening lamplight at home, focused and slightly cheeky mood. Labels: "RAW HTML" on the photocopy stack, "CLEAN TEXT" on the open register, "DISCARD" above the waste-paper basket.

key: A paper form with labelled boxes
name: ch03_form_vs_blank_sheet
alt: A bank clerk instantly spots a missing PAN box on a structured form, while a free-form blank sheet passes through and fails a week later.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves set at the same wooden bank counter with a glass partition and a small bell. LEFT panel: a neatly printed application form with labelled boxes lies on the counter; one box is clearly empty and highlighted in red. The bank clerk, a sharp woman in her forties in a navy cardigan and spectacles, taps the empty box with her pen and slides the form back to a young applicant in a striped shirt, who nods and starts filling it in. A tiny clock beside her shows only seconds passing. RIGHT panel: the same counter, but the applicant has handed in a blank sheet of paper filled with messy handwritten paragraphs in all directions; the clerk shrugs and stamps it 'received'. A small inset at the bottom right, marked with a calendar page showing one week later, shows a back-office machine jamming with that same sheet, red sparks and an error symbol. Soft fluorescent bank lighting, clean on the left and slightly chaotic on the right. Labels: "CLASS" at the top of the left panel, "DICT" at the top of the right panel, and a small tag on the empty box reading "PAN".

key: A cricket commentator who retired in 202
name: ch04_commentator_scoreboard
alt: A retired cricket commentator in the box glances at the live scoreboard for today's score while a version of him without it guesses confidently.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, the same veteran cricket commentator in both halves: a silver-haired man in his sixties in a navy blazer with a headset microphone, sitting in a glass commentary box overlooking a sunlit stadium. LEFT panel: he speaks warmly into the mic while a thought bubble above him is filled with old sepia memories of a famous batsman's cover drive and trophies, and through the glass behind him a huge electronic scoreboard clearly shows a current score with a small dotted line from the scoreboard to his eyes; he points at it while speaking, calm and accurate. RIGHT panel: the same box, but heavy blinds cover the window so the scoreboard is hidden; he speaks with exaggerated confidence, finger raised, while a speech bubble shows a wrong score with a tiny red question mark floating behind it, and a producer in the background holds his head in his hands. Bright afternoon stadium light on the left, dim enclosed light on the right. Labels: "MEMORY" beside the sepia thought bubble, "RETRIEVAL" on the scoreboard in the left panel, "HALLUCINATION" above the right panel.

key: how you find a friend's house in a new c
name: ch04_hnsw_highway_lanes
alt: A visitor finds a friend's house by taking the highway, then main roads, then walking down a lane to the exact door, shown as three stacked layers.
scene: A layered isometric illustration with three horizontal transparent planes stacked vertically like floors of a model, each showing the same city at a different zoom. TOP layer: a sparse map with a single broad highway and a few big area markers; a small white car carrying a young man in his twenties with a phone mount drives fast along it. MIDDLE layer: the same region with denser main roads and colony gates; the car turns off onto a main road toward one colony gate with a small arch. BOTTOM layer: a dense grid of narrow lanes with individual houses, potted plants and parked scooters; the young man has left the car and walks on foot to a blue house with a corner balcony where his friend waves from the door. A bold dashed red route drops vertically from the highway exit to the main road and then to the lane, with small downward arrows between layers. Next to the correct path, a slightly different exit is shown in faint grey leading to a similar-looking house one lane away, with a tiny question mark, hinting the search is approximate. Clear late-afternoon light, adventurous mood. Labels: "TOP LAYER" beside the highway plane, "LAYER 0" beside the lanes plane, and "APPROXIMATE" next to the faint grey alternative house.

key: HR screens 2,000 CVs by keyword
name: ch04_campus_hiring_rerank
alt: In campus hiring, HR rapidly screens a mountain of CVs, then a short list of candidates get a face-to-face interview.
scene: A wide two-stage illustration read left to right, connected by a funnel shape. LEFT: an engineering college seminar hall turned into a screening room, where an HR executive in her thirties in a crisp blazer sits at a long table before a towering pile of paper CVs; she quickly flicks through them with a highlighter, sending most into a large reject tray and a small number onto a 'shortlist' pile; motion lines show speed and a wall clock shows only a few minutes passed. Each CV is judged alone against a single profile sheet pinned on the wall. CENTRE: a large transparent funnel narrows from the pile of thousands to a neat stack of thirty CVs. RIGHT: a quiet interview room with a round table, where an experienced interviewer in his fifties with a salt-and-pepper beard sits across from a nervous final-year student in a formal shirt; the two face each other, talking and gesturing, with conversation lines connecting them to show they are seen together. A crumpled CV lies on the floor beside the funnel's mouth, marking a good candidate dropped early. Bright daylight on the left, warmer lamp light on the right, focused mood. Labels: "BI-ENCODER" above the CV screening table, "CROSS-ENCODER" above the interview table.

key: Packing sweets into fixed-size boxes
name: ch04_mithai_box_chunking
alt: At a mithai shop, a shopkeeper fills fixed-size boxes with whole sweets until the next one won't fit, checked on a scale, and sets aside a nearly empty last box.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view across the glass counter of a traditional Indian mithai shop, shelves behind stacked with trays of laddoos, barfi and kaju katli under warm lights. In the centre, a cheerful shopkeeper in his fifties with a white kurta, a Gandhi cap and a towel on his shoulder carefully places whole laddoos into a white cardboard sweet box of fixed size; the box is full in neat rows and he is holding one more laddoo above it, pausing because it will not fit. Three already-closed boxes tied with red string sit in a row to his left. In front of him a digital weighing scale holds one box, with a small red line on its display marking the strict weight limit. On the far right, a nearly empty last box with only two pieces sits slightly apart, and a young assistant in an apron moves it toward a bin with a small grimace. None of the sweets are cut in half. Warm golden shop lighting, glistening sugar syrup, busy festival-evening mood. Labels: "CHUNK" on the row of closed boxes, "MAX TOKENS" beside the scale's limit line, "MIN LENGTH" above the nearly empty last box.

key: A fresh graduate who has read every text
name: ch05_callcentre_sft_training
alt: A well-read graduate at a call centre first recites a manual to a customer, then after training with recorded calls answers in the company's script.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, set in a modern Indian call centre with rows of cubicles, headsets and blue carpet. The same fresh graduate appears in both halves: a lanky young man of about twenty-two with neatly combed hair, a slightly loose formal shirt and a lanyard ID card. LEFT panel: on his first day, a teetering stack of thick textbooks sits on his desk; he reads aloud from an open manual into his headset in a monotone, while a speech bubble shows a long scroll of dense paragraph lines, and a small inset of the customer on a phone shows a confused woman holding her head. RIGHT panel: two weeks later, a friendly senior trainer in her thirties in a maroon kurta sits beside him with a laptop playing a recorded call, a waveform on the screen, and a printed script card on the desk showing two short rows of arrows, one row for the customer line and one for the reply. He now speaks calmly with a confident smile, and the customer inset shows the woman nodding happily. The textbook stack is still there, unchanged, in the background. Cool office light on the left, warmer light on the right, encouraging mood. Labels: "BASE MODEL" at the top of the left panel, "AFTER SFT" at the top of the right panel.

key: A board exam paper leaks into a coaching
name: ch05_exam_leak_decontamination
alt: An examiner compares coaching-centre practice books against the sealed board exam paper and pulls out a book that contains the leaked questions.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of an examiner's office in a state education board building, steel almirahs and stacks of files in the background. In the centre, a stern but fair examiner in her fifties with grey hair in a bun, a white cotton saree and half-moon glasses sits at a large desk; in front of her lies the official exam paper in a sealed brown envelope stamped with a red wax seal, opened just enough to compare. Around her, a row of colourful practice books from coaching centres is laid out; she holds one open beside the official paper, and glowing matching lines connect identical questions on both pages. She places that book into a red tray. Through a glass partition behind her, in a coaching classroom, cheering students hold up a mark sheet showing a very high score, while a small cracked trophy sits on their teacher's desk. On the right edge of her desk, a printing-press logo stamp is crossed out on a list taped to the wall, showing the whole press is banned. Bright overhead office light, serious and investigative mood. Labels: "TEST SET" on the sealed envelope, "CONTAMINATED" on the red tray, "PROVENANCE" next to the crossed-out press list.

key: A big printed Bengaluru city map
name: ch05_lora_transparent_sheet
alt: A large printed city map stays untouched while a planner lays a thin transparent sheet with new metro lines on top, with another sheet of bus routes ready to swap in.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view of a large drafting table in a city-planning office with big windows and potted plants. Spread across the table is a huge printed city map with dense streets, lakes and parks, clamped at the corners with small metal clips and a tiny padlock icon on one clip, showing it must not be redrawn. A young urban planner in her late twenties with short hair, a denim shirt and rolled sleeves leans over the table, carefully laying a thin, clear transparent plastic sheet on top of the map; on the sheet only a few bold coloured metro lines with station dots are drawn, aligning perfectly with streets below. She holds a marker and is choosing how dark to draw a line, with a small swatch strip showing light to dark strokes. On a wall rack to the right hang two more transparent sheets, one with orange bus routes, one with green cycle lanes, ready to be swapped in. A small curved arrow shows one sheet being lifted off and another laid down. Soft natural daylight from the windows, calm and clever mood. Labels: "FROZEN W" on the printed map, "LORA ADAPTER" on the transparent sheet, "MULTI-LORA" above the rack of spare sheets.

key: Sending parcels in fixed-size courier bo
name: ch05_courier_box_packing
alt: Two courier counters: one sends each small item in its own box full of bubble wrap, the other packs three items per box with cardboard dividers.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same courier counter with a shelf of identical brown fixed-size cardboard boxes. LEFT panel: a harassed courier clerk in his thirties in a grey uniform shirt seals a row of four boxes; each box is open at the top showing one small item, a phone charger, a book, a toy car, a spice packet, surrounded by masses of bubble wrap; a long receipt curls off the counter, and a customer winces at the bill. RIGHT panel: the same clerk, now smiling, packs one box holding three small items separated by neat cardboard dividers so they cannot touch; beside it, a long rolled poster that is too tall for the box has its top end neatly trimmed off with scissors, the cut piece falling aside. Only two boxes are needed, and the receipt is short. The boxes on both sides are exactly the same size, with a ruler painted on the counter edge showing the fixed length. Bright, clean shop lighting, practical and slightly humorous mood. Labels: "PADDING" over the bubble wrap in the left panel, "PACKING" at the top of the right panel, "MASK" pointing to a cardboard divider.

key: Then the owner starts tasting two bowls
name: ch06_dhaba_dal_tasting
alt: A dhaba owner tastes two bowls of dal side by side and tells the new cook which one is better, teaching him the house style.
scene: A wide, eye-level view inside a roadside dhaba kitchen with a clay tandoor glowing in the background, steel vessels on hooks and a wooden bench. In the centre, the dhaba owner, a broad-shouldered Punjabi man in his fifties with a white kurta, a bright orange turban and a thick moustache, holds a steel spoon and tastes from one of two small steel bowls of dal placed side by side on a steel counter; he points firmly at the left bowl with a satisfied expression and waves the spoon away from the right bowl. The new cook, a nervous young man of about twenty in a vest and a checked gamcha around his neck, stands beside him holding a notebook, eagerly noting the verdict. One bowl has a glossy red tadka of ghee and chillies on top; the other looks pale and thin. Above the bowls, a small speech bubble shows a pinch-of-salt icon with a minus and a tadka-ladle icon with a plus. In a small inset in the upper left, the head cook demonstrates once at a stove while the new cook watches. Warm amber kitchen light, steam curling up, encouraging and good-humoured mood. Labels: "CHOSEN" above the left bowl, "REJECTED" above the right bowl, "SFT" on the small inset.

key: A cooking contest judge who always likes
name: ch06_biased_contest_judge
alt: A cooking contest judge is drawn to the first plate, the biggest portion and his home-state dish, while organisers shuffle plates and seat a diverse three-judge panel.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves set at a cooking contest stage with a banner-free backdrop and numbered dish plates. LEFT panel: one portly judge in his sixties with a red shawl and spectacles sits alone, reaching eagerly for the first plate in the row, which is also an oversized heap of food and a dish from his own state shown by a small regional map flag; three smaller, elegant plates further down the row are ignored. Three small tags float over his choice: a number one badge, a large-portion icon, and a home-map icon. RIGHT panel: the organiser, a brisk woman in her forties with a clipboard and headset, shuffles numbered plates into a random order with curved arrows; on the table sits a small calibration plate with a modest portion and a gold star beside it; and three judges of different ages and regional attire, a South Indian man in a veshti, a Bengali woman in a red-bordered saree and a young North-Eastern chef, taste side by side, scoring independently. Bright stage lighting, playful yet thoughtful mood. Labels: "BIASED JUDGE" at the top of the left panel, "SHUFFLE" near the curved arrows, "DIVERSE JURY" above the three judges.

key: RLHF is like hiring a food critic
name: ch06_rlhf_vs_dpo_critic_notebook
alt: Left: a food critic scores new dishes every day for a team of cooks. Right: a cook adjusts a recipe directly from a notebook of past A-beat-B verdicts, anchored by the old recipe card.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves inside the same busy restaurant kitchen. LEFT panel: a professional food critic, a sharp-dressed woman in her forties with a bob haircut and a notepad, sits at a small table while three cooks in white aprons line up and present freshly cooked dishes one by one; she holds up score cards, an 8, a 5 and a 9, and a looping circular arrow runs from the cooks to her table and back to the stoves, showing a daily cycle of cooking new dishes and scoring them. RIGHT panel: no critic; a single thoughtful cook in his thirties with a beard and white cap sits at a prep counter with an open notebook in which each line shows a small dish A sketch with a tick and dish B sketch with a cross; he is editing a recipe card with a pencil, boosting one ingredient with an up arrow and reducing another with a down arrow. Pinned above him on the wall is the old original recipe card, tied by a short elastic band to the card he is editing, so it can only stretch a little. Warm kitchen lighting, focused and clever mood. Labels: "RLHF" at the top of the left panel, "DPO" at the top of the right panel, "REFERENCE" on the pinned original recipe card.

key: Tuning a good singer's accent for a regi
name: ch06_singer_accent_beta
alt: A vocal coach gently corrects a singer's accent while reminding her to keep her natural voice; an inset shows an over-pushed version sounding like a stiff news anchor.
scene: A wide, eye-level view of a small music rehearsal room with egg-crate foam on the walls, a harmonium on a low wooden stand and a tanpura leaning in the corner. In the centre, a talented young singer in her mid-twenties, wearing a mustard kurta and jhumka earrings, sings into a studio microphone with eyes half closed, relaxed and natural. Seated beside the harmonium, her vocal coach, a gentle elderly man with white hair, round glasses and a shawl, raises one hand with thumb and finger almost touching to show a tiny correction, while his other hand rests on an old recording of her own earlier song labelled as her natural voice, tied by a short dotted line to her microphone. A single sheet of lyrics on the music stand shows one checkmark for one rehearsal. In a separate inset bubble in the upper right, a version of the same singer pushed too far stands stiffly at a news desk in a formal blazer, holding papers and reading in a flat formal tone, speech lines long and verbose, with a small warning triangle beside it. Soft warm studio lights, gentle and attentive mood. Labels: "LOW LR" next to the coach's tiny-correction gesture, "HIGH BETA" on the dotted tie to her natural recording, "OVERDONE" on the inset bubble.

key: A board-exam maths paper vs an essay pap
name: ch07_maths_vs_essay_marking
alt: Two teachers give the same mark to a maths answer but different marks to an essay until a marking scheme brings them closer.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves set in the same board-exam evaluation room with long tables, bundles of answer sheets tied with string and a ceiling fan. Two teachers appear in both halves: a tall man in his fifties with a sweater vest and a red pen, and a woman in her forties in a printed cotton saree with a green pen. LEFT panel: they each hold a copy of the same maths answer sheet showing a single boxed final answer "42"; both have written an identical tick and the same mark, and they glance at each other nodding in agreement. RIGHT panel: they each hold a copy of the same essay answer sheet covered in long paragraphs; he has written "14/20" and she has written "17/20", and they look at each other with raised eyebrows. Between them on the table lies a printed marking-scheme sheet with three short bullet rows, and a dotted arrow shows the two marks moving closer together once they read it. Soft afternoon light through tall windows, slightly humorous academic mood. Labels: "CLASSIC ML" at the top of the left panel, "LLM OUTPUT" at the top of the right panel, "RUBRIC" on the marking-scheme sheet.

key: A railway TTE checking for ticketless
name: ch07_tte_precision_recall
alt: A TTE in a train coach fines passengers; some fined passengers actually have tickets and some ticketless ones slip past, illustrating precision and recall.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view down the aisle of a crowded Indian sleeper-class coach, blue berths on both sides, luggage on racks, a window showing fields rushing by. The TTE, a stout middle-aged man in a black coat, white shirt and a name badge, stands in the aisle writing fines in a receipt book. Six passengers are visible. Three have been fined, each holding a pink fine slip: two of them are genuinely ticketless and look sheepish, while one, an indignant elderly man in a dhoti, waves a valid ticket in protest with a small red exclamation mark. Further along, two other ticketless passengers, a young man hiding behind a newspaper and a teenager crouched near the door, slip past unnoticed, each marked with a small grey ghost outline. One passenger with a valid ticket sits peacefully and is not fined. A dashed circle groups the three fined passengers. Bright daylight through the windows, gently comic mood. Labels: "PRECISION" above the dashed circle of fined passengers, "FALSE POSITIVE" next to the protesting elderly man, "MISSED" next to the two hidden passengers.

key: An open-book exam. Three things can go w
name: ch07_open_book_three_failures
alt: Three students in an open-book exam show three failures: opening the wrong chapter, ignoring the right chapter, and copying a correct but irrelevant passage.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view of an exam hall arranged as three side-by-side desks, each with a student, an open textbook and an answer sheet, plus an attentive examiner walking behind them with a clipboard. LEFT desk: a boy of about seventeen in a white school shirt has his textbook open to a chapter with a picture of a volcano while the question paper shows a picture of a plant; he writes diligently, unaware. MIDDLE desk: a girl in a school uniform and two plaits has the right chapter open beside her, pages showing the plant diagram, but she has turned her face away and is writing from memory, a thought bubble with a vague scribble above her head. RIGHT desk: a boy with spectacles copies a neat paragraph from the book word for word into his answer sheet, but the copied paragraph is about plant roots while the question asks about leaves, shown by small matching icons that clearly do not match. The examiner, a calm woman in her fifties in a cardigan, ticks three separate boxes on her clipboard. Morning sunlight through tall windows, quiet focused mood. Labels: "RETRIEVAL" above the left desk, "INTEGRATION" above the middle desk, "RELEVANCE" above the right desk.

key: Three cooks make the same dish.
name: ch07_three_cooks_comparison
alt: A five-star head chef serves a huge multi-course portion for a snack order, while a home cook serves a sensible portion that becomes tastier after feedback.
scene: A wide, eye-level illustration of three serving counters side by side, each with a cook and a plate, and one diner in front reviewing them. LEFT counter: the hotel's head chef, a grand man in his fifties in a tall white toque and double-breasted jacket, proudly presents a vast silver platter with twelve small bowls arranged in a ring, far too much food; the diner, a young woman in a casual kurta, raises her hand in polite alarm. MIDDLE counter: a home cook in her forties in a simple cotton saree and apron offers a modest plate with a single neat portion; the diner nods. RIGHT counter: the same home cook, now with a small feedback note card pinned to her apron showing a smiling face, offers a similar sensible plate garnished more carefully with a sprig of coriander; the diner smiles widely, eyes closed, savouring. A tiny scoreboard over the counters shows three very close numbers with a small wavy line to hint the gap is within noise. Warm restaurant lighting, cheerful comparative mood. Labels: "INSTRUCT" above the head chef, "SFT" above the middle counter, "DPO" above the right counter.

key: A kirana shop's credit notebook (khata)
name: ch08_khata_kv_cache
alt: A kirana shopkeeper either re-adds a regular customer's entire purchase history on a calculator or simply reads the running total in his khata and adds today's item.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves at the same small kirana shop counter with jars of toffees, a weighing scale and shelves of packets behind. The same shopkeeper appears in both halves: a plump man in his fifties with a vest, a dhoti and reading glasses on a string, and the same regular customer, a cheerful elderly lady with a cloth bag buying one packet of biscuits. LEFT panel: the shopkeeper is buried under a long paper scroll of past bills that spills off the counter to the floor, frantically punching a calculator with sweat drops, while the customer taps her foot and the wall clock spins. RIGHT panel: the shopkeeper calmly opens a thick red cloth-bound khata notebook to the customer's page, where a running total sits at the bottom; he writes one new short line below it with a pencil and smiles, transaction done in a second. On a shelf behind him stands a stack of identical blank notebooks with pre-numbered pages ready, hinting at a pre-allocated cache. Soft warm afternoon light, light-hearted mood. Labels: "NO CACHE" at the top of the left panel, "KV CACHE" on the open khata, "STATIC CACHE" on the stack of pre-numbered notebooks.

key: A shared auto-rickshaw (share auto)
name: ch08_share_auto_continuous_batching
alt: Two share autos on the same route: one rides with empty seats until everyone reaches the last stop, the other picks up a waiting person the moment a seat frees.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, each half showing the same winding city road with three bus-stop-style roadside points and the same yellow-and-black share auto with four passenger seats. LEFT panel: after the first stop, two passengers have got off and the auto drives on with two empty seats; at the roadside two people wave to flag it down, a schoolgirl with a backpack and an office worker with a tiffin bag, but the driver points ahead to the last stop and shakes his head, and empty seats are highlighted with dotted outlines. RIGHT panel: the same route; the moment a woman with a shopping bag steps off, a waiting man in a cap hops into her freed seat, and another passenger climbs in at the next point, so all four seats stay occupied; small curved arrows show passengers getting off and on at each point. At one stop the auto has paused briefly, with a tiny clock icon over it as the new passenger settles in. The driver in both panels is a cheerful man in his forties in a khaki shirt. Bright midday sunlight, lively street mood with fruit carts and pigeons. Labels: "STATIC BATCHING" at the top of the left panel, "CONTINUOUS BATCHING" at the top of the right panel, "PREFILL" next to the small clock icon.

key: Railway reservation, two ways. Contiguou
name: ch08_paged_attention_coach_bays
alt: Two train coaches: in one, families get whole long rows with many empty seats; in the other, families are spread across small bays tracked by the TTE's chart.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, each half a top-down cutaway of the same long train coach with seats in rows. LEFT panel: the coach is divided into long rows of eight seats; a young couple sits at one end of an eight-seat row with six empty seats beside them, highlighted in pale red; another row holds a family of three with five empties; scattered empty seats across the coach add up to a lot, yet a new family of four with suitcases stands on the platform outside, blocked at the door with a small no-entry sign. RIGHT panel: the same coach is divided into small four-seat bays; families fill bays in different parts of the coach, a family of six occupying one full bay at the front and another half-bay near the back, and very few seats are empty. A TTE in a black coat holds a chart with a small grid that maps each family name to bay numbers, with thin coloured lines from the chart to each bay. Two families wearing wedding outfits share one bay holding a big common pile of luggage and gift boxes. Bright daylight from the windows, orderly mood. Labels: "CONTIGUOUS" at the top of the left panel, "PAGED" at the top of the right panel, "BLOCK TABLE" on the TTE's chart.

key: the topper's paper goes to a separate re
name: ch08_llm_int8_outlier_register
alt: A teacher grades a class on a normal scale while sending one outlier topper's paper with a huge bonus score to a separate detailed register, then combines both.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a school staff room with a big wooden table, a steel cupboard and a chalkboard behind. A thoughtful teacher in her forties in a lavender cotton saree, spectacles and a pen tucked behind her ear sits at the table with two registers open. On the left, a tall pile of ordinary answer sheets with modest marks is being entered into a slim green register with neat small columns. On the right, a single answer sheet glows with a huge circled score of "1000" and a gold bonus star; she places it carefully into a separate, thick, leather-bound red register with wide, detailed columns. In a small inset at the top left, a ghosted alternative shows what goes wrong without this: a tiny grade scale from 0 to 9 squashed so that every student's sheet piles up in the lowest slot while the topper alone sits at the top. Below the two registers, two arrows converge into a final printed merit list on a clipboard. A small clock on the wall shows a little extra time passing. Soft afternoon light through barred windows, careful and methodical mood. Labels: "INT8" on the green register, "OUTLIER" on the glowing topper's sheet, "FP16" on the red register.

key: the ingredients the runner brings from t
name: ch09_caterer_runner_godown
alt: A wedding caterer's runner picks the freshest ingredients from a godown and lays them in order on the head cook's counter.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated cutaway view of a wedding catering setup, read right to left as the ingredient journey. On the RIGHT, a large dim godown with tall steel racks full of sacks, crates of tomatoes, tins of ghee and spice bags with batch tags; a quick, alert runner in his twenties, in a vest, shorts and a red cloth tied around his head, inspects a crate label with a torch, choosing the freshest batch, while an older batch with flies on it is pushed aside. A dotted path with footprints runs from the racks across a courtyard. On the LEFT, a bright outdoor kitchen under a shamiana where a master cook in his fifties, with a white apron, a big moustache and a ladle, stands at a huge kadai on a wood fire, ready to cook anything. The runner arrives and places ingredients in a neat row on the steel counter beside the cook, tomatoes, onions, spices and ghee in order, with no extra helper in between. A tiny rotten tomato has slipped into the row near the end, unnoticed by the cook. Warm evening light on the kitchen side, cooler shadows in the godown, busy and purposeful mood. Labels: "RETRIEVAL" above the runner in the godown, "AUGMENT" over the neat row on the counter, "LLM" above the master cook.

key: Searching for a lost phone in a big hous
name: ch09_torches_query_expansion
alt: One person with a torch lights a small patch of a dark hall, while three people with torches search three rooms at the same time to find a lost phone.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, each half a cutaway dollhouse view of the same large Indian house at night with the lights out, showing a hall, a bedroom, a kitchen and a study. LEFT panel: a single middle-aged man in a banian and pyjamas stands in the centre of the hall holding one torch; its beam lights only a small circle of floor near the sofa, while the rest of the house stays dark; the lost phone, glowing faintly, lies under a cushion in the study, far outside his beam. RIGHT panel: three family members each with a torch search three different rooms at the same moment: a teenage girl in the bedroom checking under the bed, the mother in a nightie in the kitchen near the fridge, and a grandfather with a walking stick in the study, whose beam lands on the glowing phone under the cushion. A small stopwatch icon floats above both panels showing the same short time. Inside the right panel, a fourth figure, a small boy, searches a bathroom with no reason to be there, a small grey noise squiggle above him. Deep blue night tones with warm yellow torch beams, mildly comic mood. Labels: "ONE QUERY" at the top of the left panel, "QUERY EXPANSION" at the top of the right panel, "NOISE" by the boy in the bathroom.

key: IPL auction scouting. A first scout filt
name: ch09_ipl_scout_rerank
alt: A scout filters thousands of cricket players by stats on a laptop, then a head coach watches videos of the thirty shortlisted players and picks five.
scene: A wide two-stage illustration read left to right inside a cricket franchise's war room. LEFT: a young data scout in his twenties in a team tracksuit sits at a laptop surrounded by floating cards of many tiny player silhouettes with stat bars; he swiftly flicks most cards into a bin, motion lines showing speed, and a small funnel on his desk narrows the cards into a short stack of thirty. CENTRE: a bold arrow carries the stack of thirty cards across. RIGHT: a quiet video room with a large screen showing a batsman's highlight clip; the head coach, a grizzled former cricketer in his fifties with a grey beard, a team cap and reading glasses, sits close to the screen with a notebook, carefully comparing each player against a single pinned sheet listing the team's exact need, a small icon of a left-arm spinner. Five player cards are pinned on a board behind him with green ticks. Two of those pinned cards show nearly identical silhouettes, both left-handed openers, with a tiny overlapping-circles icon between them, hinting he did not check for redundancy. Cool blue screen light on the left, warmer lamp light on the right, focused mood. Labels: "VECTOR SEARCH" above the scout, "RERANK" above the coach.

key: A chai stall owner with regulars.
name: ch09_chai_memory_notebook
alt: A chai stall owner who remembers only today's last few remarks forgets a regular's sugar preference, while a second version keeps a notebook line per customer.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves at the same roadside chai stall with a tin roof, a kettle on a stove, glass jars of rusks and a wooden bench. The same regular customer appears in both halves: a bespectacled office worker in his thirties wearing a blue shirt and holding a newspaper. LEFT panel: the chaiwala, a friendly man in his forties with a checked shirt and a towel on his shoulder, hands over a glass of very sweet tea with heaped spoons of sugar; above his head a thought bubble shows only three small speech bubbles from today, and the customer grimaces at the first sip. RIGHT panel: the same chaiwala consults a small, dog-eared pocket notebook open beside the stove, where one line under a small face sketch shows a sugar cube with a minus and a ginger root crossed out; he pours a perfect light-sugar chai and the customer smiles. A tiny smudged, half-erased line at the bottom of the notebook page hints that a summary can lose a detail. Early morning light with steam rising, warm and friendly mood. Labels: "SHORT-TERM" at the top of the left panel, "SUMMARY MEMORY" on the notebook in the right panel.

key: An auto-rickshaw vs a shared jeep
name: ch10_auto_vs_shared_jeep
alt: At a station exit, an auto-rickshaw leaves immediately with one passenger while a shared jeep waits until ten passengers board.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of the dusty forecourt outside a small-town Indian railway station, the station building with a clock tower in the background. LEFT: a single yellow-and-green auto-rickshaw is already pulling away with motion lines and a puff of dust, carrying one young woman in a salwar kameez with a small suitcase; a stopwatch icon above it shows almost no waiting time. RIGHT: a large old jeep with a canvas roof and luggage tied on top is parked, its driver, a burly man in his forties in a white shirt and sunglasses, leaning on the bonnet and calling out for passengers; seven people are already squeezed inside, two more climb in, and one last man with a sack hurries toward it. A stopwatch above the jeep shows a longer wait, and a small counter by the jeep reads "10". Small icons of people stacked beside the jeep show many passengers per trip versus a single icon beside the auto. Bright, hot afternoon light with long shadows, lively mood. Labels: "LOW LATENCY" above the departing auto, "HIGH THROUGHPUT" above the shared jeep.

key: Three ways a sweet shop serves
name: ch10_sweet_shop_three_modes
alt: A sweet shop serves fresh jalebis at the counter, hands out tokens on a busy festival day, and stacks pre-packed mithai boxes on a shelf.
scene: A wide, eye-level view of a large, busy Indian sweet shop on a festival evening with marigold strings and fairy lights, composed in three zones left to right. LEFT: at the front counter a halwai in his fifties with a white vest and a flowing moustache fries orange jalebi spirals in a big kadai of hot oil while a little boy and his father stand watching, waiting right there, the boy's eyes wide. CENTRE: a token counter where a young cashier in a red kurta hands a numbered paper token to a woman in a bright saree who is turning away to sit on a bench and look at her phone; above the counter a digital display shows a token number being called, with a small chime icon. RIGHT: tall glass shelves stacked with closed, ribbon-tied mithai boxes packed the night before; a customer in office clothes simply picks one off the shelf and walks to the door, with a small moon-and-stars icon on the shelf label to show they were packed overnight. Golden festival lighting, steam and sparkle, cheerful and crowded mood. Labels: "REAL-TIME" above the jalebi counter, "ASYNC" above the token counter, "BATCH" above the shelves of boxes.

key: A dhaba where one cook does everything
name: ch10_tandoor_separate_services
alt: A dhaba cook juggles chopping, billing and the tandoor while it goes cold, versus a restaurant with a dedicated tandoor station and a separate prep and billing counter.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a cramped roadside dhaba where a single harried cook in his thirties, in a vest and a gamcha around his neck, tries to do everything at once: he chops onions with one hand, scribbles a bill with the other, and balances a plate on his elbow, sweat flying; behind him a clay tandoor has gone dark and cold, with a small snowflake icon and a rupee coin icon with a falling arrow beside it, showing the expensive oven sitting idle. RIGHT panel: a neat restaurant kitchen divided into two stations by a pass-through window: on one side a tandoor glows bright orange and a specialist tandoor cook in a white cap slaps rotis onto its walls non-stop; on the other side two cheaper helpers in aprons chop vegetables, plate food and run a billing machine; a plate slides across the window between the stations, with a tiny lightning-bolt icon on the window to hint the hand-off is a network call. Warm dim light on the left, bright organised lighting on the right. Labels: "MONOLITH" at the top of the left panel, "GPU" above the glowing tandoor, "BUSINESS SERVICE" above the prep and billing side.

key: A toll plaza on the highway. At 3 a.m.
name: ch10_toll_plaza_autoscaling
alt: A highway toll plaza with one booth open at night and all booths open on a festival weekend, with a marshal waving cars to the next free booth.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same wide highway toll plaza from a slightly elevated front angle, with a long canopy over many booths. LEFT panel: deep night under a starry sky and a crescent moon, a wall clock on the canopy showing three o'clock; only one booth is lit with a green light while all the others are dark with red crosses; a single truck passes through. RIGHT panel: bright festival-weekend daylight with marigold decorations on the canopy, every booth lit green with an operator in each; a long, colourful line of cars, SUVs with luggage on top and buses with families approaches; in front of the booths a marshal in a reflective vest and white gloves waves each car toward the next free booth with a baton, small arrows fanning out from him. On the far right of the right panel, one new booth is still being switched on by a technician, its light flickering amber with a small hourglass icon, showing that new capacity takes time. Clean highway signage with no text other than labels. Labels: "REPLICAS" above the row of booths in the right panel, "LOAD BALANCER" next to the marshal, "WARM-UP" by the flickering booth.

key: dev is the cook trying a new dish
name: ch11_kitchen_dev_staging_prod
alt: A restaurant kitchen where a cook tries a new dish at the back, staff taste it at their evening meal, the head chef checks it, and a waiter carries it to a customer.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated cutaway view of a restaurant read left to right in three zones. LEFT, the back counter: a young cook in his twenties with a white cap experiments with a new paneer dish in a small pan, spices scattered, a recipe register open beside him with dated entries. MIDDLE, the staff dining table: at a plain table with steel plates, four staff members in aprons taste small portions of the dish at the evening staff meal, one giving a thumbs up, one adding salt. At the pass between the kitchen and the dining room, a stern head chef in his fifties with a tall toque and folded arms inspects every plate under a heat lamp, a small green tick stamp in his hand. RIGHT, the dining room: a smart waiter in a black waistcoat carries the approved plate straight out to a happy couple at a candle-lit table, without anyone calling him, with small motion lines. On a shelf above the back counter, the dated recipe register shows earlier versions with tabs, and a small curved arrow points back from the dining room to an older tab, hinting at rollback. Warm golden restaurant lighting, professional and confident mood. Labels: "DEV" above the back counter, "STAGING" above the staff table, "PRODUCTION" above the dining room.

key: Airport security. The input guard
name: ch11_airport_guardrails
alt: Passengers pass X-ray and frisking before boarding and customs checks on arrival, with several counters running in parallel.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves set in a bright modern Indian airport with tall glass walls and planes visible outside. LEFT panel: the departure security area, where three security lanes run side by side in parallel; passengers place bags on X-ray belts, a monitor shows the outline of a suitcase with one sharp object highlighted in red, and a security officer in her thirties in a uniform and beret pulls that item out into a tray; another officer frisks a traveller with a handheld wand. RIGHT panel: the arrival customs hall, where two green-channel counters work in parallel; a customs officer in his forties with a moustache checks a passenger's opened bag and sets aside a suspicious package, while other travellers with trolleys flow through. Between the panels, a tiny plane icon arcs over the dividing line to show the journey. In a small inset at the bottom right, an innocent traveller holding a harmless coconut is mistakenly stopped, with a small question mark, hinting that guards sometimes flag innocent items. Clean bright daylight, calm but vigilant mood. Labels: "INPUT GUARD" at the top of the left panel, "OUTPUT GUARD" at the top of the right panel, "PARALLEL" over the side-by-side lanes.

key: Packing for a trip in a suitcase with la
name: ch11_suitcase_docker_layers
alt: An open suitcase shown in cross-section with clothes at the bottom and the boarding pass and snacks on top, compared with a traveller unpacking everything because the pass is at the bottom.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, each half showing a large open suitcase in clean cross-section like a layered cake, on a bed in a hotel-style room. LEFT panel: the layers stack neatly from bottom to top: folded clothes, a pouch of toiletries, a pair of shoes in a bag, a row of books, and right on top a boarding pass and a packet of snacks. A relaxed young woman in her late twenties in a travel jacket swaps only the boarding pass and snacks on top with one hand, while the lower layers stay untouched, with small lock icons beside each lower layer. RIGHT panel: the same suitcase but the boarding pass is buried under the clothes at the very bottom; a frustrated young man in a T-shirt has pulled every layer out onto the bed, clothes, shoes and books strewn everywhere, to reach the pass, sweat drops on his forehead, with a curved arrow showing that everything above has to be repacked. A wall clock in the right panel shows much more time passing than in the left. Soft morning light from a window, light-hearted mood. Labels: "BASE IMAGE" on the clothes layer in the left panel, "YOUR CODE" on the boarding-pass layer in the left panel, "REBUILD ALL" at the top of the right panel.

key: An electricity meter for each flat.
name: ch11_electricity_meter_tokens
alt: A row of flat electricity meters in an apartment building where one meter spikes sharply and the society app flags it before the bill arrives.
scene: A wide, eye-level view of the ground-floor meter room of an Indian apartment society, a whitewashed wall with a neat row of eight electricity meters in grey boxes, each with a small flat-number plate and a spinning dial. Seven meters show calm, steady small bars on tiny graphs floating above them. One meter in the middle shows a sharply rising red bar with an upward arrow and a small figure of "+80%". In the foreground the society secretary, a brisk retired gentleman in his sixties with a cardigan, white moustache and a smartphone, looks at his phone, which shows a notification bell beside a small meter icon. Through a doorway at the right, a glimpse of that flat shows two possible causes side by side: a newly installed split AC on the wall, and a sparking wire behind a cupboard. A wall calendar beside the meters shows the bill date still far away. In a small faded corner inset, a string of festival lights on a balcony hints that some spikes are seasonal and legitimate. Cool fluorescent light in the meter room, alert but calm mood. Labels: "TOKEN METER" above the row of meters, "ALERT" beside the secretary's phone, "SEASONAL" on the festival-lights inset.

key: Paying the electricity bill. Tier 1
name: ch12_bill_payment_tiers
alt: Three stages of paying an electricity bill: queuing at the office, automatic UPI payment, and a bank's own pipeline testing a new app version.
scene: A three-panel horizontal illustration separated by thin vertical lines, read left to right as three levels of automation. LEFT panel: a long queue outside a government electricity office window on a hot day; a middle-aged man in a white shirt and spectacles stands holding a paper bill and an umbrella for shade, looking at his watch, with several people ahead of him. MIDDLE panel: the same man relaxes on a sofa at home sipping tea, while his phone on the side table shows a payment-done tick and a small calendar icon and a small envelope icon, showing it pays on a date or when the bill arrives; a dotted line runs from the phone toward a tiny electricity pylon. RIGHT panel: inside a bank's tech office, a young engineer in her twenties with a lanyard watches a large screen showing a simple pipeline of three boxes with green ticks, a new app version moving through tests to a row of phones, while the man's autopay tile on one phone remains unchanged with a green tick. Hot harsh sunlight on the left, cosy indoor light in the middle, cool blue screen light on the right. Labels: "MANUAL" above the left panel, "CT" above the middle panel, "CI/CD" above the right panel.

key: Checking a new auto-rickshaw meter.
name: ch12_auto_meter_behaviour_tests
alt: An inspector tests an auto-rickshaw meter three ways: same route with a different driver shirt, a longer route costing more, and the base fare staying right.
scene: A three-panel horizontal illustration separated by thin vertical lines, each showing the same yellow-and-green auto-rickshaw with a large black fare meter, and the same inspector, a precise woman in her forties in a khaki uniform with a clipboard. LEFT panel: two side-by-side snapshots of the same driver on the same short route, once in a blue shirt and once in a red shirt; both meters show the exact same fare, and the inspector ticks her clipboard. MIDDLE panel: a small road map with two routes from the same start, a short green route and a long winding orange route; the meter for the long route shows a clearly higher number with an upward arrow, and she ticks again. RIGHT panel: the auto stopped just past a roadside marker stone at the first stretch; the meter shows the base fare and a small checkmark, with the inspector holding up a printed reference card showing the same number. The driver in all panels is a friendly man in his fifties with a grey moustache. In the background of each panel, the meter's casing is opaque so its insides cannot be seen. Bright midday street light, methodical and good-humoured mood. Labels: "INVARIANCE" above the left panel, "DIRECTIONAL" above the middle panel, "MINIMUM" above the right panel.

key: A chaiwala who learned his trade near a
name: ch12_chaiwala_drift
alt: A chaiwala near a college sees three changes: office workers replacing students, half his sales becoming cold coffee, and students now asking for green tea.
scene: A three-panel horizontal illustration separated by thin vertical lines, each showing the same small chai stall under a neem tree across the road from a college gate, and the same chaiwala, a cheerful man in his forties with a checked shirt, a towel on his shoulder and a big steel kettle. LEFT panel: the college gate behind is closed with a padlock, and instead of students a group of office workers in formal shirts, lanyards and laptop bags crowd the stall; the chaiwala looks surprised at the new faces. MIDDLE panel: his counter now shows half the cups as tall plastic glasses of cold coffee with ice, and a small sales tally board beside him shows a split bar, half brown and half pale; he scratches his head. RIGHT panel: the college gate is open again and the same familiar students with backpacks and notebooks are back, but each is pointing at a jar of green tea leaves while his masala chai kettle sits untouched, with a little sweat drop on his forehead. A tiny graph icon above each panel shows a curve shifting. Warm late-afternoon light, gently comic mood. Labels: "DATA DRIFT" above the left panel, "TARGET DRIFT" above the middle panel, "CONCEPT DRIFT" above the right panel.

key: fire alarm that goes off every time some
name: ch12_toast_fire_alarm
alt: A building fire alarm rings over toast and residents ignore it, until one day there is a real fire and still nobody reacts.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, both halves showing a cross-section of the same small apartment building with three floors. LEFT panel: in a ground-floor kitchen, a young man in a T-shirt and boxer shorts lifts a slightly browned slice of toast from a toaster; a faint wisp of smoke reaches a ceiling smoke detector, which flashes red with big zig-zag sound lines. On the floors above, residents react with boredom: an elderly lady in a nightgown rolls her eyes and puts on earmuffs, a student at a desk pulls a pillow over his head, and a small wall calendar shows many ticked days in a row. RIGHT panel: a real fire with orange flames and thick smoke spreading from a top-floor room; the same alarm flashes and rings, but the residents still ignore it, the lady reading with earmuffs on and the student asleep under his pillow; only a small cat at the window looks alarmed. A faint dial icon next to the detector in the left panel shows its sensitivity needle set too high. Warm morning light on the left, dramatic orange glow on the right, cautionary mood. Labels: "FALSE ALARMS" at the top of the left panel, "REAL INCIDENT" at the top of the right panel, "THRESHOLD" beside the dial icon.
